concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: Trailblazer Copilot for Teams
Thesis: A native Microsoft Teams bot that proactively connects first-years with upperclassmen based on hidden CLR overlaps, executing seamless intros.
Why this frame: This represents the most direct, frictionless execution of the concept: a conversational interface embedded in the tool students already use daily, fully automating the matching and introduction logic without requiring a new platform.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Maya
  Role: First-Year Undergraduate Student
  Context: Six weeks into her first semester, Maya is overwhelmed by club fairs and course selections, unsure which choices actually lead to her desired co-op outcomes.
  Emotional state: Anxious about falling behind her peers but intimidated by the idea of cold-messaging alumni on LinkedIn.
  Pain points:
    - Lacks an informal network to give her the 'inside scoop' on which clubs matter.
    - Fears reaching out to upperclassmen because she doesn't know what to say.
    - Overwhelmed by generic advice that doesn't apply to her specific academic track.
    - Hates filling out profile forms on new networking apps.
  JTBD: Find a relatable peer who has successfully navigated my exact situation so I can copy their playbook.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Upperclassman Mentor: Receives an automated Teams message asking if they are open to a quick chat with a matched first-year.
  - Central Co-op Administrator: Monitors aggregate connection metrics via a Power BI dashboard to ensure equitable distribution of matches.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: The moment Maya receives a proactive Teams notification from the NU Copilot suggesting a high-confidence peer match based on her recently enrolled courses and club attendances.

USE CASES (5) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Proactive Match Notification
     Trigger: Power Automate detects a new high-confidence vector match in Snowflake between Maya's early CLR data and an upperclassman's historical year-one data.
     Flow: Maya receives a native Teams Adaptive Card. She reads the shared attributes (e.g., 'You both took CS2500 and joined Data Club'). She clicks 'Learn More'.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro translates the raw Snowflake vector distance into a warm, natural language explanation of the overlap.
     Outcome: Maya understands exactly why this specific person is relevant to her.
  2. Drafting the Icebreaker
     Trigger: Maya clicks 'Request Introduction' on the Adaptive Card.
     Flow: A modal appears. Copilot generates three distinct conversation starters based on the shared CLR data. Maya selects one and tweaks the tone to be more casual. Maya hits send.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.6 (via Copilot wrapper) synthesizes the shared entities into contextual, low-pressure opening messages.
     Outcome: Maya overcomes the blank-page anxiety of networking.
  3. Mentor Acceptance
     Trigger: Upperclassman receives the intro request in their Teams.
     Flow: Upperclassman reviews the match rationale, clicks 'Accept & Say Hi'. A shared Teams chat is instantly spun up with Maya's icebreaker.
     AI role: None directly in this step; relies on Power Automate routing.
     Outcome: A private, 1:1 peer mentorship channel is established.
  4. AI-Guided Follow-up
     Trigger: Two weeks pass since the initial Teams chat was created.
     Flow: The Copilot bot pings Maya privately: 'Did you end up chatting with Sam? Here are some questions you could ask about their upcoming co-op.' Maya clicks a prompt to drop it into the chat.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro analyzes the chat transcript to determine if the conversation stalled, generating context-aware follow-ups.
     Outcome: The connection is sustained beyond a single 'hello'.
  5. Opt-Out / Pause Matching
     Trigger: Maya feels she has enough guidance for now.
     Flow: Maya types 'pause matches' to the bot. The bot confirms and updates her status in the Snowflake database. The bot offers a 'resume in Spring' button.
     AI role: Basic NLP intent recognition via Microsoft Copilot.
     Outcome: Maya retains control over her notification volume without navigating complex settings.

KEY SCREENS (5) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Teams Chat Canvas — purpose: The primary interface for interacting with the Trailblazer bot.
     Primary element: Chronological feed of Adaptive Cards containing match profiles.
     Motion character: Standard Microsoft Teams native motion; snappy and familiar.
  2. Match Rationale Adaptive Card — purpose: To explain the 'why' behind the match.
     Primary element: A visual Venn diagram or bulleted list showing overlapping courses, clubs, and skills.
     Motion character: Subtle fade-in of overlapping attributes to build trust.
  3. Icebreaker Copilot Modal — purpose: To facilitate the first message.
     Primary element: Three AI-generated message bubbles and a free-text edit box.
     Motion character: Shimmering text effect as Copilot types out the suggested messages.
  4. Active Connections Tab — purpose: A static tab within the Teams app to manage ongoing peer relationships.
     Primary element: Grid of connected upperclassmen with 'Last interaction' timestamps.
     Motion character: Smooth list transitions.
  5. Feedback Micro-survey Card — purpose: To capture qualitative outcomes for the co-op office.
     Primary element: A simple thumbs up/down and one-tap tags (e.g., 'Helpful advice', 'Didn't respond').
     Motion character: Card collapses into a 'Thank You' checkmark upon selection.

AI CAPABILITIES (3) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. CLR Vector Similarity Search
     User action: Implicit (Maya enrolls in a course or swipes into a club event).
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro (Embeddings)
     Input: Maya's real-time Snowflake record vs. Upperclassmen's historical Year-1 records.
     Output: A ranked list of top 5 most similar upperclassmen profiles.
     User benefit: Zero manual data entry; the system knows her path automatically.
  2. Match Rationale Translation
     User action: Maya views a new match card.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.6
     Input: JSON payload of overlapping CLR nodes.
     Output: A two-sentence, empathetic explanation of why this peer is relevant.
     User benefit: Transforms cold database linkages into a warm, human introduction.
  3. Contextual Icebreaker Generation
     User action: Maya clicks 'Draft Message'.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Shared CLR attributes + Upperclassman's current co-op employer.
     Output: Three varied text drafts (e.g., Casual, Direct, Question-focused).
     User benefit: Removes the primary friction point of networking for introverted students.

SEED DATA — generate the FULL count of records per entity (not 1-3 example shapes — the actual full set):
  PRIMARY ENTITIES (2):
    • FirstYearStudents — target_count 25
      Shape: { student_id: string, major: string, courses_in_progress: string[], clubs: string[], vector_embedding: float[] }
      Example records summary: First-year students with 1-2 completed courses, 1-3 club affiliations, no co-op history yet. Formatted with anonymized IDs, majors ranging from Khoury CS to D'Amore-McKim Business.
    • UpperclassmenMentors — target_count 40
      Shape: { mentor_id: string, name: string, year_1_courses: string[], year_1_clubs: string[], coop_employer: string, opt_in_status: boolean, capacity_remaining: number }
      Example records summary: Juniors and Seniors who have completed at least one co-op. Includes their historical Year-1 footprint (what they looked like back then) and their current success state.
  SECONDARY ENTITIES (1):
    • CLR_Nodes — target_count 15
      Shape: { node_id: string, type: string, display_name: string }
      Example records summary: Specific courses (e.g., CS2500, BUSN1101) and clubs (e.g., Data Club, Women in Finance) used to build the overlap rationale.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Native Microsoft, accessible, conversational, understated, reassuring
  Hero treatment: The Adaptive Card inside Teams—it must look like a standard Microsoft UI component but enriched with dynamic, AI-generated personalization.
  Motion character: Utilitarian and snappy, matching the host OS (Teams).
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Generate a realistic screenshot of a Microsoft Teams dark-mode interface featuring an Adaptive Card labeled 'Trailblazer Match'.
    2. Generate a subtle, abstract background image used in the header of the Adaptive Card representing 'connection' and 'data points merging'.

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Stage 5 audits the prototype against each of these):
  - The interface is entirely contained within Microsoft Teams.
  - The match rationale explicitly references at least two shared CLR data points (e.g., course + club).
  - The user never types their own profile data (zero manual entry).
  - The icebreaker drafts are distinct in tone and contextually relevant.
  - No visual language implies scoring, ranking, or 'red' readiness indicators.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
  Brand: NU
  Platform: web
  Accessibility: WCAG AA
  Other:
    - Must use Microsoft Teams UI patterns
    - Must honor FERPA (no exposing grades, only enrolled courses/clubs)

=== CONSULTING BRIEF (every field below is mandatory grounding for the prototype) ===
Thesis: Connects first-year undergraduate students with upperclassmen mentors who share identical early-stage CLR profiles and successfully landed aspirational co-ops.
Description (what gets built):
Utilizing the CLR data, this tool operationalizes the 'Trailblazer' concept at scale. Microsoft Copilot analyzes the first-year student's emerging CLR profile and searches the historical Snowflake database for upperclassmen who had highly similar profiles during their own first year. It identifies students who subsequently secured high-value co-ops. The tool then facilitates a lightweight introduction via Microsoft Teams, providing conversation starters based on their shared background. This creates a scalable, peer-to-peer mentorship network that requires zero manual profile creation.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students rely heavily on informal networks, but introverted or first-generation students often lack access to these whispers. This addresses Theme 4: Alumni as Trailblazers and Mentors, democratizing access to peer wisdom and reducing isolation.
How it supports first-year undergraduate students outcomes over first 18-24 months:
Students who engage with peer mentors exhibit higher retention and make more strategic early-career choices, leading to a measurable increase in first-cycle co-op match rates and reduced advisor dependency.
CLR dependency / independence rationale:
The matching algorithm depends entirely on the granular skill, course, and club data housed within the CLR. Without this deep, verified dataset, the matches would be superficial (e.g., matching just by major), which fails to build the necessary rapport.
Execution within Northeastern University's existing stack (named systems, connectors, AI layer location):
The matching engine runs on Snowflake data, orchestrated by Power Automate. The user interface and introduction mechanism occur entirely within Microsoft Teams, utilizing the existing NU Source framework if salvageable, or bypassing it entirely in favor of native Teams chat.
Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, Power Automate, Power BI fit (named tools that reduce cost/burden):
By executing the introductions natively in Microsoft Teams, this concept sidesteps the need to procure or repair a standalone mentorship platform, aligning strictly with Jen's cost containment and ecosystem directives.

brief.one_line_thesis: A native Microsoft Teams bot that proactively connects first-years with upperclassmen based on hidden CLR overlaps, executing seamless intros.

primary_persona.name: Maya
primary_persona.context: Six weeks into her first semester, Maya is overwhelmed by club fairs and course selections, unsure which choices actually lead to her desired co-op outcomes.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Anxious about falling behind her peers but intimidated by the idea of cold-messaging alumni on LinkedIn.

secondary_actors.involvement: Receives an automated Teams message asking if they are open to a quick chat with a matched first-year.
Monitors aggregate connection metrics via a Power BI dashboard to ensure equitable distribution of matches.

brief.demonstrated_moment: The moment Maya receives a proactive Teams notification from the NU Copilot suggesting a high-confidence peer match based on her recently enrolled courses and club attendances.
jobs_to_be_done: Find a relatable peer who has successfully navigated my exact situation so I can copy their playbook.
success_criteria: The interface is entirely contained within Microsoft Teams.
The match rationale explicitly references at least two shared CLR data points (e.g., course + club).
The user never types their own profile data (zero manual entry).
The icebreaker drafts are distinct in tone and contextually relevant.
No visual language implies scoring, ranking, or 'red' readiness indicators.

other: Must use Microsoft Teams UI patterns
Must honor FERPA (no exposing grades, only enrolled courses/clubs)

screens.purpose: The primary interface for interacting with the Trailblazer bot, showing the initial state before a match is found.
screens.persona_state: Anxious about falling behind, overwhelmed by choices, but comfortable in the familiar Teams environment.
content_blocks: Microsoft Teams Left Sidebar (Chat, Teams, Calendar)
Trailblazer Copilot Chat Header

motion_contract.encodes: Builds trust by visually demonstrating the overlap; circles slide together and the intersection glows slightly.

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Background vector search completes (simulated on load)
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a matching engine. Given a first-year student's current courses and clubs, find the most similar upperclassmen based on their historical year-1 data.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Find matches for Maya (Courses: CS2500, MATH1341; Clubs: Data Club) against the upperclassmen database.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: JSON array of top 5 mentor_ids with similarity scores.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an empathetic peer advisor. Translate raw overlapping data points into a warm, two-sentence explanation of why this upperclassman is a good mentor for this first-year student.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Translate this overlap: Student A and Student B both took {shared_courses} and joined {shared_clubs} in their first semester. Student B is now at {employer}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a networking assistant helping an introverted first-year student draft a Teams message to an upperclassman. Generate 3 distinct, low-pressure conversation starters based on their shared background.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Draft 3 icebreakers for Maya to send to Sam. Shared background: {shared_courses}, {shared_clubs}. Sam's current co-op: {employer}. Tones: 1 Casual, 2 Direct, 3 Question-focused.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a relationship management bot. Analyze the metadata of a connection and suggest a contextual follow-up question to keep the mentorship active.
ai_flows.user_message_template: It has been 14 days since Maya and Sam last chatted. Sam works at {employer}. Suggest one short follow-up question Maya could ask Sam.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an intent recognition router. Determine if the user wants to pause notifications, resume notifications, or ask a question.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: JSON object with 'intent' (enum: pause, resume, question) and 'confidence_score'.

critique.summary: The prototype is excellent, capturing the Teams native feel and correctly implementing the AI flows with multi-provider fallbacks and verbalized sampling. However, it contains a blocking violation: buttons without an onClick handler in the Active Connections tab. I have added a global toast system to wire up these dead buttons and fulfill the spec's success toast requirement.

issues.description: The 'Message' buttons in the Active Connections tab lack onClick handlers.
issues.source_of_truth: Depth & AI Checklist (Rule 2: 'Are there onClick={() => {}} or buttons with no handler? -> BLOCKING.')
issues.fix: Implemented a global toast notification system in the App root and wired the 'Message' buttons to trigger a toast, simulating opening a chat.

issues.description: The Icebreaker Copilot Modal navigates to the Active Connections tab without showing the required success toast.
issues.source_of_truth: Interaction Spec (State Machine: icebreaker_copilot_modal -> active_connections_tab side effects)
issues.fix: Wired the handleSend function to trigger the newly added global toast with the message 'Message sent to Sam!' before navigating.
